subsystems.name: Excitation laser
subsystems.role: shines a narrow, monochromatic beam onto the sample; the tiny fraction of light that scatters inelastically carries the chemical fingerprint.
parts: diode or VCSEL laser, commonly 785 nm or 1064 nm

subsystems.name: Probe optics
subsystems.role: delivers the laser to the sample and collects the faint scattered light while blocking the much brighter unshifted laser light.

subsystems.name: Spectrograph
subsystems.role: spreads the collected light into a spectrum so each Raman shift falls on a different detector element.
parts: volume holographic or ruled diffraction grating

subsystems.name: Detector
subsystems.role: converts the very weak spectrum into electrical signal with low noise.
parts: deep-depletion silicon CCD (visible/NIR) or indium gallium arsenide array (1064 nm)

subsystems.name: Embedded computer and library
subsystems.role: identifies the substance by comparing the measured spectrum against stored reference spectra.
parts: matching algorithm (for example correlation or hit-quality index)

subsystems.name: Calibration and self-test
subsystems.role: keeps the wavelength axis and intensity response honest between services.

buildSteps.title: Choose the laser wavelength
buildSteps.detail: A shorter wavelength gives a stronger Raman signal but excites more sample fluorescence; 785 nm is the common compromise, while 1064 nm sacrifices signal to avoid fluorescence in coloured or biological samples.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and align the optical bench
buildSteps.detail: The laser, filters, lenses and grating are mounted on a rigid bench and painstakingly aligned so the laser spot and the collection path overlap on the sample.

buildSteps.title: Build the spectrograph
buildSteps.detail: The grating and slit are chosen to give roughly 8–15 cm⁻¹ resolution over the fingerprint region, enough to distinguish most organic compounds.

buildSteps.title: Fit and cool the detector
buildSteps.detail: The CCD or InGaAs array is bonded to a thermoelectric cooler in a sealed package, since the signal from a single laser shot is extremely weak.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the wavelength axis
buildSteps.detail: Known standards — a polystyrene film with its sharp peak near 1001 cm⁻¹, or a gas-discharge lamp — are used to map detector pixels to Raman shift.

buildSteps.title: Load and validate the spectral library
buildSteps.detail: Reference spectra of thousands of compounds are measured on the same instrument type and tested against blind samples so matching thresholds are trustworthy.

buildSteps.title: Package for field use
buildSteps.detail: The optics go into a sealed, drop-tested housing with a class 3B laser enclosure, interlock, battery and simple point-and-shoot interface.

buildSteps.title: Verify against laboratory methods
buildSteps.detail: Field results are checked against laboratory infrared or mass-spectrometry analysis to quantify false positives and false negatives.

pathway.milestone: handheld Raman units used for hazardous-material identification, pharmaceutical raw-material checks and mineral or gemstone testing
pathway.unlocks: laboratory-grade identification at the point of need, in seconds and without consumables.

pathway.milestone: through-container and standoff variants, plus spatially offset sampling to suppress fluorescence
pathway.unlocks: scanning sealed drums, bags and vials safely, without opening them.

pathway.milestone: deep-ultraviolet excitation and further optical miniaturisation
pathway.unlocks: stronger signals from small samples and clearer spectra from materials that currently fluoresce.

pathway.milestone: merged multi-technique sensors with machine-learning interpretation
pathway.unlocks: one handheld tool that covers elements, molecules and trace residues, and moves Raman toward clinical and food-safety testing.
